The further out we project, the more external factors can influence the outcome, making precise predictions more challenging.

While our 90% confidence intervals capture a wide range of probable outcomes, certain significant risks or "black swan" events could push actual results outside these bounds. These are typically high-impact, low-probability events that lie beyond the scope of typical probabilistic modeling reflected in these intervals.
